correctness.rationale: The proof uses the established regular-polygon secondary polytope and its face-poset dual. Two area-weighted identities plus its known full dimension identify the exact real translation module by removing Fourier frequencies zero and one. Equivariant radial projection identifies the simplicial sphere with the unit sphere in that module. Each remaining complex weight from 2 through (p-1)/2 is nonzero modulo the odd prime p, giving a free action and precisely the claimed weighted lens space. The standard integral lens complex gives homology and fundamental group for p>=7, with p=5 treated separately. A standalone complete orbit-chain calculation verifies p=5 and p=7, including the order-seven Smith factor and primitive third boundary; the general proof does not depend upon the finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The new claim classifies the ordinary full cyclic orbit space and its exact lens weights, rather than just a fixed (invariant) polytope, ambient sphere, or the topologically different cyclohedron. Inspected Reiner Proposition 4.2 classifies fixed secondary polytopes, not ordinary cyclic quotient boundaries. Fomin-Zelevinsky classify classical type-A/B sphere complexes, not this orbit-space homeomorphism type. Earlier indexed cyclohedral lens quotients use a different Fourier representation and do not imply the omission of the first nontrivial harmonic in the polygonal type-A case. Explicit literature and database searches yielded no equivalent claim. Priority risk from short unindexed corollaries remains.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed consequence of equivariant fiber-polytope geometry may identify the same quotient without using the phrase associahedral lens space.

value.rationale: A natural complete topological classification of the rotational quotient of each odd-prime polygonal associahedral sphere; precise weights determine the lens homeomorphism class rather than merely ranks. The first nontrivial case L(7;2,3) has seven-torsion in degree one. As p grows, the quotient develops order-p integral torsion in arbitrarily many odd degrees even though the covering spaces are integral spheres; the omitted first Fourier mode is a geometrically motivated invariant specific to type A, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
